logistics.format: 72-hour hands-on advanced exploit-development practical exam plus 24-hour report

formal: OSCE3 designation (which itself requires OSEP+OSWE+OSED) is the conventional milestone before OSEE.

third_party_evaluations.summary: Recognised in EU/UK red team and exploit-dev community.

evaluation.rationale: Independent reviews of the stored evidence produced expert: 1, specialty: 2. The existing unordered-specialty rule applies when at least one reviewer identifies a specialty track. See each persona rationale for the supporting factors and limitations.

hiroshi-tanaka.rationale: The recorded 72-hour practical and advanced kernel/browser exploitation establish exceptional exploit-research depth; the explicit niche audience makes specialty more informative than broad enterprise rank despite expert peer hints.

maria-okonkwo.rationale: The 72-hour kernel and browser exploitation practical demonstrates exceptional depth in exploit research. Its narrow audience makes specialty the most informative placement, and the conventional OSCE3 milestone should not be treated as an enforced prerequisite.

alex-novak.rationale: The recorded 72-hour practical across advanced kernel and browser exploitation, with a report and strong top-tier peer recognition, demonstrates exceptional offensive depth. That sustained assessment supports expert placement despite the five-year profile and niche audience.
